_note: Description prose for the C&B pieces whose export body was a bare spec list. Every number here is read off that list - carat, diamond count, millimetres - and nothing is invented: no clasp, no setting and no stone the export does not state. Applied by import-cb-export.mjs --copy, which inserts the Description above the list the product already has and labels that list Key Features.
AJPD263:
A single round brilliant lab-grown diamond and a polished initial disc, set a little apart from each other along an 18 inch chain rather than gathered at the centre.

The initial is 8.2 mm across - large enough to read, small enough to wear to work. Ask us for the letter you want when you order.
AJLB223:
A 0.75 carat marquise lab-grown diamond, 9.19 by 4.79 mm, set lengthways into a solid Cuban link chain.

The links do most of the work; the stone sits flush among them and catches the light only when your wrist turns. A heavier bracelet than it looks in photographs.
AJLB222:
One oval lab-grown diamond of 0.75 carats, 7.32 by 5.13 mm, set into a Cuban link chain.

Rounder and softer than the marquise version, and the shape most people reach for first. Worn alone it reads as a chain bracelet with a secret.
AJLB221:
A 0.67 carat emerald cut lab-grown diamond, 6 by 4 mm, set into a Cuban link chain.

The emerald cut's long open table gives flashes rather than sparkle, which suits the flat planes of the links around it. The quietest of the three Cuban link bracelets.
AJLB206:
Eighty-one round brilliant lab-grown diamonds, 1.9 mm each, running the full length of the bracelet for a total of 2.19 carats.

Small stones set close together read as one continuous line of light rather than a row of separate diamonds. The everyday weight of tennis bracelet - 5 g in 14K - and the one to start with.
AJLB200:
Sixty-nine round brilliant lab-grown diamonds at 2.4 mm each, 4 carats in total, set in an unbroken line around the wrist.

A step up in stone size from the 2 carat line, and it shows: the individual diamonds are large enough to pick out, and the bracelet throws light from across a room.
AJLB161:
Sixty oval lab-grown diamonds, 3.6 by 2.6 mm each, 6 carats laid end to end around the wrist.

Ovals sit longer in their settings than rounds do, so the line reads as a ribbon rather than a row of dots. Worth seeing in person.
AJLB157:
Thirty-three pear cut lab-grown diamonds of 5.75 by 3.75 mm, 9.9 carats in all, each one pointing into the next.

The pears are set nose to tail, which gives the bracelet a direction most tennis lines do not have. A statement piece that still lies flat.
AJLB152:
Thirty-five emerald cut lab-grown diamonds, 6 by 4 mm each, totalling 19.5 carats.

Nearly 20 carats of long rectangular stones set shoulder to shoulder, and the weight to match: 16.2 g in 18K gold. This is the one for the occasion you will be photographed at.
AJLB167:
Fifty-six emerald cut lab-grown diamonds at 4 by 2.8 mm, 11.2 carats around the wrist.

Smaller stones than the 19.5 carat line and a finer bracelet for it - the emerald cut's steps are still clearly visible, but it sits close to the skin.
AJLB26:
Forty pear cut lab-grown diamonds, 6.5 by 4.5 mm each, 20 carats in total.

The heaviest bracelet we make: 22.3 g of 18K gold before the stones. The pears alternate direction along the line, so it moves with the wrist instead of sitting stiff.
AJLB130:
Thirty-eight lab-grown diamonds in two cuts - 5 by 2.5 mm baguettes with 2.9 mm round accents between them - 5.93 carats in all.

The baguettes give straight lines of light and the rounds break them up. An art deco pattern without the costume-jewellery weight.
AJLB53:
A single marquise lab-grown diamond, 10.5 by 5.25 mm and a full carat, bezel-set on a fine chain.

The bezel's rim is what makes it wearable: nothing to catch on a sleeve, and the stone sits flat against the wrist. The longest-looking of the four solitaire bracelets.
AJLB54:
One emerald cut lab-grown diamond of 1 carat, 7.2 by 4.8 mm, held in a plain bezel on a fine chain.

A rectangle of light and a thin line of metal, and nothing else. For anyone who finds prongs fussy.
AJLB52:
A 1 carat pear cut lab-grown diamond, 9.1 by 5.6 mm, bezel-set and hung from a fine chain.

The point of the pear follows the line of the chain, so the stone lies along the wrist rather than across it.
AJLB51:
One oval lab-grown diamond, 8.2 by 5.75 mm and a full carat, set in a close bezel on a fine chain.

The oval is the easiest of these shapes to wear every day, and the bezel means you can wear it without thinking about it.
AJLB160:
Two hundred and sixty-two round brilliant lab-grown diamonds, 1.05 carats between them, pavé-set across the faces of a Cuban link chain.

Every link is covered, so there is no metal left showing from the top. Up close you can see the individual stones; from arm's length it is a band of white light.
AJLB118:
Sixteen round brilliant lab-grown diamonds at 3.1 mm each, 2 carats in total, on an adjustable bolo chain.

The bolo closure pulls to any size, so it can sit tight at the wrist or loose over a cuff - and it is the one bracelet here you can put on one-handed.
